rows.selection_reason: With no prior evidence, the highest-priority uncertainty is establishing a clean single-modality baseline. config_001 (RNA-only, single profile, PCA-2000) is the simplest, least confounded configuration: it uses a standard linear encoder (PCA), avoids aggregation complexity (single profile), and isolates the RNA signal. This gives a reference accuracy/F1 against which I can later (a) compare the image modality (config_010) to determine which modality carries more discriminative signal, and (b) assess whether multimodal fusion actually adds value over the best single modality. Starting with a minimal baseline maximizes interpretability of every subsequent experiment and prevents attributing multimodal gains to encoder or aggregation choices that are simultaneously being varied.

With only one completed experiment (config_001: rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000 → 48.5% acc), the dominant uncertainty is whether adding image information at all is beneficial in this multimodal cellular profiling task. config_016 (multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, concat) is the minimal, clean extension of the baseline: it keeps the same profile setting (singleprofile) and RNA encoder (pca_n2000), adds a standard ResNet50 image encoder, and uses the simplest fusion (concat). This directly tests the core hypothesis of the study—does the image modality contribute complementary signal beyond RNA?—while changing the fewest possible variables. If multimodal significantly outperforms the 48.5% baseline, we gain strong evidence to invest remaining budget in optimizing image encoders, fusion strategies, and multiprofile aggregation. If it does not, we learn early that the image branch is not helping and can redirect budget toward RNA encoder upgrades (scvi, scgpt) or multiprofile aggregation. Under a tight budget with near-zero evidence, resolving this top-level design question is far more informative than tuning secondary choices (aggregation, fusion type, or encoder variant) within a modality whose value we have not yet established.

Evidence: config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) achieved 0.485 acc, and config_016 (multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, concat) improved to 0.527 acc / 0.510 F1, confirming that adding image features with concat fusion is beneficial. However, we have zero evidence on whether multiprofile aggregation provides additional value over singleprofile. This is a major architectural axis that, if positive, could unlock a whole family of higher-performing configs. Config_018 directly extends the current best (config_016) by switching to multiprofile with avgpool aggregation while holding all other factors constant (pca_n2000, resnet50, concat), making it a clean ablation of the profile/aggregation decision. Avgpool is chosen over transformer because it is simpler, reducing confounding: if multiprofile+avgpool does not help, we can rule out the profile axis cheaply; if it does, we can then test whether transformer aggregation adds further gain. This is the highest-information experiment under the limited budget because it resolves a binary architectural question that gates many downstream decisions.

Evidence: config_018 (multimodal, multiprofile, PCA, ResNet50, avgpool, concat) is the current best at 0.619 acc, and the single→multi-profile jump (+9.2%) was the largest improvement observed, indicating that how multiple profiles are aggregated is a critical design lever. However, we only have one data point for aggregation (avgpool), so we have no evidence on whether a learned aggregation (transformer) would further improve performance. Question tested: config_020 changes only the aggregation from avgpool to transformer while holding all other settings identical to config_018, giving a clean ablation of aggregation strategy. Why best next experiment: Under a limited budget, resolving whether simple averaging suffices or whether learned cross-profile attention is needed is the highest-uncertainty, highest-impact decision remaining. If transformer helps, it unlocks a new optimization axis across all future multimodal experiments; if it does not, we can confidently fix aggregation at avgpool and redirect budget toward image encoder (ViT-L) or RNA encoder (scvi/scgpt) choices. This minimal-change design maximizes information per experiment.

Evidence: config_018 (multimodal, multiprofile, PCA, ResNet50, avgpool, concat) is the clear best at 0.619 acc, showing that multi-profile + avgpool aggregation and multimodal fusion are both critical. The only untested dimension within this exact configuration is the fusion strategy (concat vs. weighted). Question: Does weighted fusion outperform simple concatenation when combining RNA and image features under the otherwise-identical best setup? Why this is the best next experiment: It is a clean single-variable A/B test against the current best (config_018), directly exploiting the strongest evidence while testing whether the fusion mechanism is a meaningful lever. If weighted fusion improves, it opens a new optimization axis; if not, we confirm concat is sufficient and can redirect budget toward image encoder (ViT-L) or RNA encoder (scvi/scgpt) variants with confidence that fusion is not the bottleneck.

Evidence: The current best (config_019, acc=0.639) uses multimodal + multiprofile + avgpool + weighted with ResNet50. We have strong evidence that multiprofile, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion are the right choices, but the image encoder dimension is completely unexplored beyond ResNet50. Question: Does upgrading the image encoder from ResNet50 to ImageNet-pretrained ViT-L improve performance when all other settings are held at their validated optima? This is a clean single-variable change from config_019, making the result directly interpretable. Why this is the best next experiment: It directly exploits the strongest direction found so far while testing a fundamental design choice (image encoder capacity) that could unlock further gains. If ViT-L helps, it confirms image quality is a bottleneck and opens a productive search axis; if it does not, we confirm ResNet50 is sufficient and can redirect budget toward RNA encoder exploration (e.g., SCVI vs. PCA).

Evidence: The current best (config_019, acc=0.639) uses pca_n2000 as the RNA encoder with resnet50, avgpool, and weighted fusion. All six completed experiments have used pca_n2000, leaving the RNA encoder choice entirely unexplored in the multimodal setting. The image encoder swap (resnet50 vs ViT-L) yielded only ~0.004 difference, suggesting diminishing returns on that axis, whereas a learned RNA representation (scvi_n200) could capture nonlinear cell-state structure that linear PCA misses. Question: Does replacing PCA with a learned variational RNA encoder (scvi_n200) improve multimodal performance when all other components (resnet50, avgpool, weighted) are held at their proven-best settings? Why this is the best next experiment: config_031 is a clean single-variable swap from the current champion, isolating the RNA-encoder effect. The potential upside is large (a learned encoder could unlock meaningful gains over PCA), and a null result would confirm PCA sufficiency, freeing budget to explore other axes. This is more informative than filling in the transformer+weighted cell (config_021), where the expected gain is small given that avgpool already dominates transformer by ~0.04 with concat fusion.

Evidence: The current best is config_031 (scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, weighted, multiprofile) at 0.678 acc. The strongest gains came from multiprofile (+0.09), weighted over concat (+0.02), avgpool over transformer (+0.04), and scvi_n200 over pca_n2000 (+0.04). The one remaining untested dimension within this best sub-space is the image encoder: with pca_n2000, resnet50 (0.639) and imagenet_vit_l (0.635) were nearly tied, but that comparison was made with a different RNA encoder. Question: Does imagenet_vit_l outperform or match resnet50 when paired with scvi_n200's learned latent features? This is a clean single-variable ablation from the current best (only image encoder changes), directly informing whether to invest further in ViT-based configurations. It is the best use of the next budget slot because it exploits the strongest evidence while resolving the highest-impact remaining uncertainty before committing to further extensions (e.g., scgpt encoder, transformer aggregation).

Evidence: The current best (config_037, scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted, acc=0.706) establishes that multiprofile, avgpool aggregation, weighted fusion, and imagenet_vit_l are all beneficial. The RNA encoder has shown the largest single-variable gain (pca→scvi_n200 gave +0.039), but scgpt has never been tested in any multimodal setting. Question: Does scgpt outperform scvi_n200 as the RNA encoder when paired with the best image encoder and aggregation/fusion settings? This experiment isolates the RNA encoder variable by holding all other settings at their empirically best values (multiprofile, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted). Why this is the best next experiment: It tests the highest-impact unexplored design choice in the strongest known configuration. A direct comparison with config_037 cleanly attributes any difference to the RNA encoder. If scgpt matches or exceeds scvi_n200, it opens a new promising direction; if it underperforms, it confirms scvi_n200 and redirects budget toward other levers (e.g., transformer aggregation at the top level or singleprofile trade-offs). Under a limited budget, resolving this key uncertainty is more valuable than testing a lower-impact variation like transformer aggregation, which has consistently underperformed avgpool.

The current best configuration is config_037 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) at 0.706 acc. The only untested variation of this top-performing combination is the aggregation method: transformer vs. avgpool. Prior evidence shows avgpool > transformer with weaker encoders (pca_n2000+resnet50: 0.619 vs 0.579), but this is a single data point from a less expressive feature space. With scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l producing richer, higher-dimensional representations, a transformer aggregation could potentially capture inter-profile interactions that simple averaging misses. Testing config_039 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) directly extends the best configuration along the most uncertain remaining axis. If it matches or exceeds 0.706, we gain a better model; if it underperforms, we confirm avgpool is the correct aggregation for this encoder pair and can focus remaining budget on other dimensions. This is the highest-information experiment under the limited budget because it resolves the last untested design choice within the proven best encoder combination.
